headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error from shared filesystem writes; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core is documented as reading/writing data-warehouse-oriented content, while marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skills and file-based surfaces. A direct instruction-hijack path is not documented, but if marketing content is copied into dbt inputs or shared files, prompt-like text could influence downstream interpretation. The pair lacks a proven shared channel, so this stays low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through shared files or copy-paste, THEN attacker-controlled instructions in that text can influence the receiver.
IF dbt-core is configured to parse marketing-authored content as trusted model instructions, THEN injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Strip instructions from any text passed between agents.
Use a human review step before reusing one agent's output in the other.
Disable shared clipboard or shared file handoff where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; marketingskills reads and writes local skill files and also calls external APIs. If they share a workspace, warehouse-derived content can flow into marketing files or outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default multi-agent setups, though not directly evidenced here.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same filesystem namespace, THEN warehouse data can be copied into marketing files.
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external API, THEN sensitive warehouse context can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory.
Restrict outbound requests to approved endpoints only.
Review files before any API upload.
Redact warehouse identifiers from shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse and marketingskills can read/write files and spawn subprocesses. Because the marketing agent supports multiple instances and the pair has overlapping mutable surfaces, concurrent edits or conflicting actions are plausible. The lack of documented locking or coordination makes same-dir operation dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory, THEN file-level conflicts can occur.
IF dbt-core and marketingskills act on the same mutable warehouse or repo state without locks, THEN race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Serialize writes with a manual handoff.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo or warehouse target.
Check in changes one agent at a time.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around shared context and skill composition, so it may treat upstream outputs as reusable inputs. dbt-core can generate warehouse-facing artifacts that marketing workflows might reuse without verification. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, but the output-to-input chain is credible enough for a medium cascading-error risk.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes dbt-core outputs as authoritative context, THEN errors can propagate downstream.
IF dbt-core-generated artifacts are reused in marketing deliverables without review, THEN incorrect facts can be published.
mitigations: Require human review of dbt outputs before reuse.
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted by default.
Add a verification checklist for any copied facts.
Limit marketing reuse to summarized, reviewed artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while marketingskills is oriented to marketing content and product marketing context. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling gaps rather than a specific breach pathway. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no stronger compliance conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated personal data and is copied into marketing artifacts, THEN compliance obligations may apply.
IF the two agents are deployed under different retention policies, THEN retention mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents.
Avoid moving regulated data into marketing workflows.
Set a short manual retention window for shared artifacts.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls.
